learning.tasks-title: Competencies to practice in this file:
learning.topic-directives-what-is: Directives are classes in Angular that add new behaviors, transform HTML layout, or modify DOM elements. There are two primary types: Structural Directives (@if, @for, @switch, <ng-template>) which add or remove DOM nodes, and Attribute Directives (ngClass, ngStyle, routerLink, ngModel) which change the styling or behavior of existing elements.
learning.topic-directives-what-use: Used to make views reactive and conditional without manual DOM scripting. For example, conditionally toggling loading spinners and alerts (@if), rendering dynamic product or user lists (@for), applying active CSS classes or color themes (ngClass, ngStyle), and navigating between views (routerLink).
learning.topic-binding-what-is: Data Binding is the communication bridge between a TypeScript component class (data state) and its HTML template (user view). Angular provides 4 core binding types: Interpolation ({{ }}), Property Binding ([prop]), Event Binding ((event)), and Two-Way Binding ([(ngModel)]).
learning.topic-binding-what-use: Used to build interactive user interfaces where the view automatically updates when data changes, and user inputs instantly update component state. For example, displaying variable values in headers, disabling submit buttons while loading ([disabled]), handling click and submit events, and two-way syncing form inputs.
learning.topic-forms-what-is: Template-Driven Forms use directives directly inside HTML templates (FormsModule, #form="ngForm", and [(ngModel)]) to handle input capture and validation. Angular automatically generates an internal form control tree corresponding to the inputs in the template.
learning.topic-forms-what-use: Used for simple or standard forms (like login, sign-up, feedback, or search bars) where validation requirements are straightforward and you want to write minimal TypeScript code while letting Angular manage validation states (.valid, .invalid, .touched, .submitted).
learning.topic-reactive-forms-what-is: Reactive Forms provide a programmatic, model-driven approach where form structure and validations are defined explicitly in TypeScript using FormGroup, FormControl, and Validators, and bound to HTML via [formGroup] and formControlName.
learning.topic-reactive-forms-what-use: Used for complex, dynamic, or enterprise forms that demand strict validation logic, immutability, reactive observable data streams, unit testing, and dynamic fields (e.g. multi-step registration, dynamic address lines, or async username checks against an API).
learning.topic-router-what-is: Angular Router is the Single Page Application (SPA) navigation system that maps browser URL paths to components and renders them dynamically in <router-outlet> without refreshing the entire webpage.
learning.topic-router-what-use: Used to create organized, bookmarkable multi-view web applications, enforce authentication route guards, pass route parameters, and trigger smooth view transitions via routerLink buttons or programmatic router.navigate() redirects.
